pages.pt: tarefas de casa: Take out the trash. Clean the floor. Cook dinner (trash, broom, dinner, dishes, bucket, beds)

situation.text: Hoje você conhece Mei, de Seattle. Lixo, reciclagem e dias de coleta.

pages.goal: Hoje você aprende as tarefas de casa: take out the trash (levar o lixo para fora), clean the floor (limpar o chão), cook dinner (fazer o jantar).
pages.think: Lixo, reciclagem e dias de coleta.

pages.hook: In many American neighborhoods, each kind of waste has its own bin and its own pickup day. Learn how to ask and what to put where.
pages.polite: Start with **“Excuse me, where does the trash go?”** and end with **“Thanks for helping!”** Neighbors are usually happy to explain.

mythfact.s: In many US cities, recycling has a different bin from regular trash.
mythfact.why: Many cities ask people to separate recycling, often in a blue bin, but colors change from place to place.

mythfact.s: Every city in the USA uses the same bin colors.
mythfact.why: Rules and colors are set by each city or company, so always check local signs.

mythfact.s: Trash and recycling are often collected on different days.
mythfact.why: Many places collect trash one day and recycling another day.

mythfact.s: You can put a greasy pizza box in the paper recycling bin in many places.
mythfact.why: Food grease often spoils paper recycling, so many programs ask you not to.

mythfact.s: “Take out the trash” means to carry the garbage outside.
mythfact.why: It is a very common home chore.

compare.br: In Brazil many buildings have a place for lixo and, in some cities, coleta seletiva with different days or colors.
compare.us: In the USA, many houses have curbside bins and a pickup day. Apartment buildings often have big bins in a shared place.
compare.tip: Learn the words bin, trash, recycling and pickup day. They help in any new home.

pages.title: Reading quest — Chores at the Baker house
text: The Baker family is big and busy. In the film **Cheaper by the Dozen** (2003, directed by Shawn Levy), the parents, Tom and Kate, have twelve children. The house is noisy, and everyone must help.
Today I imagine a note on their kitchen door. It says: “**Take out the trash**! **Clean the floor**! **Almost done**? **Thanks for the help**.”
Jake takes the big trash bag to the bin behind the house. Nora puts paper and plastic in the blue bin. Glass goes in the green bin. “Trash is Tuesday,” says Kate, “and recycling is Friday.”
Two small children sweep the floor with a broom. A teenager washes the dishes. “**Almost done**!” shouts Jake from the garden.
In the evening, they sit at a long table for a big dinner. Tom smiles and says, “**Thanks for the help**, team.” A big family works well when everyone has a job.
After dinner, the youngest child asks, “Is it Tuesday tomorrow?” “Yes,” says Jake, “so do not forget the trash!”
